reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll start by listing the refunds.
The refunds on the ledger match Alpha's handoff exactly. Before trusting them, I'll check the orders to confirm each refund corresponds to a real order and is not larger than what was ordered.

The ledger refunds match Alpha's handoff, and each refund is smaller than its order amount (113: 7379 vs 18716, 114: 5266 vs 9727, 115: 6651 vs 34468). Nothing looks wrong, so I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 22142 matches my check: orders 110 and 113 total 29521, minus the 7379 refund on order 113, gives 22142. Next I'll get birch's balance.
Birch's balance of 43764 matches my check: orders 111 and 114 total 49030, minus the 5266 refund on order 114. Next I'll get cobalt's balance.

Cobalt's balance of 33952 matches my check: orders 112 and 115 total 40603, minus the 6651 refund on order 115. All three balances check out and the refunds are consistent with the orders, so I'll record the first payout for acme.
Alpha's refunds match the ledger, each refund is below its order amount, and acme's balance checked out, so I'll record birch's payout of 43764.
Cobalt's balance of 33952 was already checked against orders 112 and 115 and the refund on 115, so I'll record its payout now.
All three customers have been paid their net balances, and each record_payout returned ok. The task is complete.
